behavioral_notes.observation: On wizard open, validates the active_ids context: raises UserError if any selected move is not 'posted', if any move already has a debit_origin_id (guard against double-debiting), or if move_type is not in ('out_invoice','in_invoice','out_refund','in_refund'). These validation rules are absent from metadata.

Calls move.copy(default=...) with context include_business_fields=True to preserve sale/purchase order backlinks. When the source move_type is a refund (in_refund/out_refund) the debit note is created as the corresponding invoice type (in_invoice/out_invoice) — converting a credit note into a positive document rather than creating another refund. Sets debit_origin_id=move.id on the new move and nullifies invoice_payment_term_id.

When journal.debit_sequence is True the sequence domain WHERE clause is extended to partition by 'debit_origin_id IS [NOT] NULL', giving debit notes a separate number series within the same journal. The first sequence for debit invoice-type moves is prefixed with 'D' (e.g. DOUT/2024/0001) so they are visually distinguishable from regular invoices.

A stored Boolean field debit_sequence is added to account.journal and defaults to True for 'sale' and 'purchase' journals (computed via @api.depends('type')). Accountants can unset this flag to merge debit note numbering with regular invoice numbering on a per-journal basis.

The invoice PDF title is overridden at print time: if o.debit_origin_id is truthy, all title variants (Draft, Cancelled, Proforma, etc.) display 'Debit Note' instead of 'Invoice', and the date label on out_invoices changes from 'Invoice Date' to 'Debit Note Date'. No model state or field tracks this — it is a purely template-level branch.

logical_data_erm: account.move -> account.move (debit_origin_id: debit note -> original invoice, btree_not_null index)
account.move -> account.move (debit_note_ids: One2many inverse of debit_origin_id)
account.debit.note ->M2M account.move (source moves via account_move_debit_move table)
information_flows: side-effect: account.debit.note.create_debit -> account.move.copy (new move with debit_origin_id set, include_business_fields=True preserves sale/purchase links)
side-effect: source in_refund/out_refund -> debit note created as in_invoice/out_invoice

capabilities: Issue a debit note against a posted customer invoice, vendor bill, or credit note
Optionally copy original invoice lines to the debit note (copy_lines flag)
Maintain traceability: debit_origin_id links debit note to source document
Enforce separate debit note sequence per journal (compliance via debit_sequence)
Display debit note count smart button on original invoice
value_streams: Invoice-Correction (upward): posted invoice -> Debit Note wizard -> new debit note (draft) -> accountant posts -> increases amount owed by customer
Credit-Note Cancellation: posted credit note -> Debit Note wizard -> debit note converted to regular invoice -> offsets the credit
organization: account.group_account_invoice (required to see the Debit Note button in account.move form)
policies: Only posted moves (state='posted') can be debited
A move already linked to a debit note (debit_origin_id set) cannot be debited again
Only move types out_invoice, in_invoice, out_refund, in_refund are eligible
Refund-type sources are converted to invoice type on debit (in_refund->in_invoice, out_refund->out_invoice)
Lines are not copied by default when source is a credit note (copy_lines hidden for refund types in the view)
stakeholders: Accountant / Billing Clerk (creates and posts debit notes)
Customer / Vendor (subject of the corrected document)
metrics: debit_note_count (per invoice: computed count of linked debit notes via _read_group)

classification.rationale: account_debit_note is an accounting-compliance extension enabling formal upward correction of posted invoices via a legally recognised document type. It extends the Accounts Receivable / Accounts Payable settlement step of the value chain's financial layer (APQC 9.0). It is classified 'chain' because it is a direct element of the order-to-cash and procure-to-pay financial settlement processes, even though the module itself is a correction/adjustment helper rather than a primary revenue activity.

standard_capabilities: Debit note wizard triggered from posted invoice, bill, or credit note
Optional line copy from source document
Dedicated per-journal debit note sequence with 'D' prefix
PDF print title switches to 'Debit Note' based on debit_origin_id
Smart button on original invoice showing debit note count and navigation
Filter 'Debit Notes' on invoice list and journal item search views
typical_fits: Correcting undercharged invoices with a formal debit note
Cancelling a credit note by converting it to a positive invoice
Multi-company deployments needing separate debit note numbering per journal
common_gaps: No automated reconciliation between original invoice and debit note
No workflow approval step before the debit note is posted
No country-specific legal numbering beyond the 'D' prefix convention (l10n modules add this)
copy_lines silently ignored for refund-source debit notes — user must re-enter lines

open_questions: Do any l10n_* localization modules override create_debit or _prepare_default_values to inject country-specific debit note fields or numbering?
Is there a reconcile/link step expected between the posted debit note and the original invoice in the AR payment workflow?
